Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most talked‑about releases from the past few weeks (and a few that are hitting theaters soon). I’ve grouped them by genre and added a brief note on why they’re worth watching.

| Release | Genre | Release Date | Why It’s Hot |
|---------|-------|--------------|--------------|
| **“Dune: Part Two”** | Sci‑Fi / Action | **July 20, 2026** | The epic sequel to Denis Villeneuve’s 2021 “Dune.” Fans are eager to see how the story wraps up and the stunning visuals continue. |
| **“The Marvels”** | Superhero | **July 28, 2026** | A crossover featuring Captain Marvel, Ms. Marvel, and Monica Rambeau. Marvel’s biggest fan‑service event of the year. |
| **“Oppenheimer” (re‑release)** | Historical Drama | **July 15, 2026** | Christopher Nolan’s biopic about J. Robert Oppenheimer is back in limited release after a successful run in 2023. |
| **“The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes”** | Fantasy / Adventure | **August 5, 2026** | A prequel to the original Hunger Games trilogy, exploring the origins of the Games. |
| **“Spider‑Man: Across the Spider‑Verse”** | Animation / Action | **August 12, 2026** | The third film in the Spider‑Verse franchise, praised for its animation style and emotional depth. |
| **“The Last Voyage of the Demeter”** | Horror | **July 22, 2026** | A fresh take on the Dracula myth, focusing on the ship that carried the vampire to America. |
| **“The Woman King” (re‑release)** | Historical Action | **July 18, 2026** | A re‑release of the 2022 film starring Lupita Nyong’o, now available in 4K HDR. |
| **“The Exorcist: Believer”** | Horror | **August 2, 2026** | A new chapter in the Exorcist saga, directed by David Gordon Green. |
| **“The Last of Us” (Movie Adaptation)** | Drama / Thriller | **August 10, 2026** | A film adaptation of the hit video game, starring Pedro Pascal and Bella Ramsey. |
| **“The Great Wall” (Reboot)** | Fantasy / Action | **July 30, 2026** | A reboot of the 2016 film, now with a new cast and updated CGI. |

### How to Catch Them

- **Theaters** – Most of these titles are still playing in major chains (AMC, Regal, Cinemark). Check your local listings for showtimes.
- **Streaming** – Some titles (e.g., “Oppenheimer” re‑release) will be available on HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video within a week of theatrical release.
- **Special Events** – Keep an eye out for midnight premieres or fan‑meet events, especially for the Marvel and Spider‑Man films.

If you’re looking for something more niche—like indie dramas, documentaries, or foreign cinema—just let me know and I can dig up the latest releases in those categories!
